Well, I don't do Mac, but I do BSD, from which OSX was developed. BSD is really clumsy about resizing filesystems, so unless OSX has some utility to make shrinking your primary partition super easy, you're probably just better off sticking with a USB install unless/until you're comfortable doing a full install on the machine and blowing away OSX. But if there is such a tool, the process would be the same as any other system: shrink the primary partition down to give yourself twenty or more GB at the end of your drive, and install Kali there; GRUB will handle figuring out how to boot the individual operating systems as necessary.

If you're stuck with the USB and still want persistence, it should be noted that you can install to a USB device, which the system will boot to and identify as /dev/sda. The only really tricksy bit about this is that if you use a USB installer to do it, you can end up with config files that point to /dev/sdb1 for some resources, because that's where your "boot drive" was during install, after you remove the install media, so unless you're comfortable booting into single user mode to edit these files manually, it's best to do the install via DVD.
